verses.sloka: अथ शैलाद्विनिष्क्रम्य मैथिलीं कोसलेश्वर: ।अदर्शयच्छुभजलां रम्यां मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् ॥ २.९५.१॥
verses.transliteration: atha śailādviniṣkramya maithilīṁ kosaleśvara: ।adarśayacchubhajalāṁ ramyāṁ mandākinīṁ nadīm ॥ 2.95.1॥

translations.english: Then Rama, the lord of Kosala, descended from the mountain and showed Sita the charming river Mandakini of sacred waters.
translations.hindi: अपने परिवार के लोगों और साथ्रियोंसद्ित भरत जी, भरद्वाज जी की ऐसी राजसी ठाठ की पहुनाई भें बह रात बिता, सबेरा होते ही, राम दर्शन की कामना से, भरद्वाज जी के पास विदा मॉगने गए

verses.sloka: अब्रवीच्च वरारोहां चारुचन्द्रनिभाननाम् ।विदेहराजस्य सुतां रामो राजीवलोचन: ॥ २.९५.२॥
verses.transliteration: abravīcca varārohāṁ cārucandranibhānanām ।videharājasya sutāṁ rāmo rājīvalocana: ॥ 2.95.2॥

translations.english: Lotus-eyed Rama said to the heavy-hipped daughter of the king of Videha, whose face resembled the beautiful Moon.
translations.hindi: पुरुषसिंह भरत को हाथ जोड़े अपने सामने खड़ा देख, अग्निहोत्र सम्बन्धी नई विधि विधान के पूरा कर, भरद्वाज जी ने उनसे कहा

verses.sloka: विचित्रपुलिनां रम्यां हंससारससेविताम् ।कमलैरुपसम्पन्नां पश्य मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् ॥ २.९५.३॥
verses.transliteration: vicitrapulināṁ ramyāṁ haṁsasārasasevitām ।kamalairupasampannāṁ paśya mandākinīṁ nadīm ॥ 2.95.3॥

translations.english: Look at this enchanting river Mandakini with its variegated sandbanks frequented by geese and swans and adorned with lotuses.
translations.hindi: हे अनघ ! यह तो मुझे बतलाओ कि मेरे आश्रम मे पिछली रात सुख से तो कटी ! तुम्हारे साथ के सब लोग मेरे आतिथ्य से भली भाँति सन्तुष्ट ते हैं ?

translations.english: See this river sparkling with trees of every kind laden with fruits and flowers growing on its banks. Everywhere it resembles the lake Nalini of Kubera.
translations.hindi: यह कहते हुए तेजस्वी महर्षि भरद्वाज जब आश्रम से बाहिर आए, तब भरत जी ने हाथ जोड़ कर, उनको प्रणाम किआ ओर बोले

verses.sloka: मृगयूथनिपीतानि कलुषाम्भांसि साम्प्रतम् ।तीर्थानि रमणीयानि रतिं सञ्जनयन्ति मे ॥ २.९५.५॥
verses.transliteration: mṛgayūthanipītāni kaluṣāmbhāṁsi sāmpratam ।tīrthāni ramaṇīyāni ratiṁ sañjanayanti me ॥ 2.95.5॥

translations.english: The herds of deer have just drunk water by descending down the landing places and the waters are still turbid. This sight produces great pleasure in me.

verses.sloka: जटाजिनधरा: काले वल्कलोत्तरवासस: ।ऋषयस्त्ववगाहन्ते नदीं मन्दाकिनीं प्रिये ॥ २.९५.६॥
verses.transliteration: jaṭājinadharā: kāle valkalottaravāsasa: ।ṛṣayastvavagāhante nadīṁ mandākinīṁ priye ॥ 2.95.6॥

translations.english: O my beloved rishis with matted locks and wearing deer skins and bark of trees as upper cloth bathe in the river Mandakini for performing morning ablutions in time.

verses.sloka: आदित्यमुपतिष्ठन्ते नियमादूर्द्ध्वबाहव: ।एते परे विशालाक्षि मुनय: संशितव्रता: ॥ २.९५.७॥
verses.transliteration: ādityamupatiṣṭhante niyamādūrddhvabāhava: ।ete pare viśālākṣi munaya: saṁśitavratā: ॥ 2.95.7॥

translations.english: O largeeyed Sita, some other ascetics of rigid austerities worship the sungod according to tradition, lifting up their arms and invoking the Sun.

verses.sloka: मारुतोद्धूतशिखरै: प्रनृत्त इव पर्वत: ।पादपै: पत्ऺत्रपुष्पाणि सृजद्भिरभितो नदीम् ॥ २.९५.८॥
verses.transliteration: mārutoddhūtaśikharai: pranṛtta iva parvata: ।pādapai: patऺtrapuṣpāṇi sṛjadbhirabhito nadīm ॥ 2.95.8॥

translations.english: With the trees whose tops are swayed by the wind, the mountain was as if dancing, shedding leaves and flowers all around the river.
Behold this river Mandakini whose waters here are transparent like crystals, there sparkling with sand dunes and elsewhere crowded with siddhas.

verses.sloka: निर्द्धूतान् वायुना पश्य विततान् पुष्पसञ्चयान् ।पोप्लूयमानानपरान् पश्य त्वं जलमध्यगान् ॥ २.९५.१०॥
verses.transliteration: nirddhūtān vāyunā paśya vitatān puṣpasañcayān ।poplūyamānānaparān paśya tvaṁ jalamadhyagān ॥ 2.95.10॥

translations.english: Look at the scattered heaps of flowers shaken off by the wind and large quantities of flowers floating on the waters.

verses.sloka: तांश्चातिवल्गुवचसो रथाङ्गाह्वयना द्विजा: ।अधिरोहन्ति कल्याणि विकूजन्त: शुभा गिर: ॥ २.९५.११॥
verses.transliteration: tāṁścātivalguvacaso rathāṅgāhvayanā dvijā: ।adhirohanti kalyāṇi vikūjanta: śubhā gira: ॥ 2.95.11॥

translations.english: O my auspicious Sita, sweetvoiced Chakravaka birds singing in most pleasant tones are alighting on those heaps of flowers.

verses.sloka: दर्शनं चित्र कूटस्य मन्दाकिन्याश्च शोभने ।अधिकं पुरवासाच्च मन्ये च तव दर्शनात् ॥ २.९५.१२॥
verses.transliteration: darśanaṁ citra kūṭasya mandākinyāśca śobhane ।adhikaṁ puravāsācca manye ca tava darśanāt ॥ 2.95.12॥

translations.english: My lovely Sita, I consider watching this mount Chitrakuta and river Mandakini in your presence more delightful than living in Ayodhya.

The waters of river Mandakini is perpetually agitated by siddhas who are endowed with asceticism, selfrestraint and tranquillity and who are cleansed of sins by taking bath in the river. Plunge with me into this river.

verses.sloka: सखीवच्च विगाहस्व सीते मन्दाकिनीं नदीम् ।कमलान्यवमज्जन्ती पुष्कराणि च भामिनि ॥ २.९५.१४॥
verses.transliteration: sakhīvacca vigāhasva sīte mandākinīṁ nadīm ।kamalānyavamajjantī puṣkarāṇi ca bhāmini ॥ 2.95.14॥

translations.english: O lovely Sita, like a companion plunge into this river Mandakini, submerging the red and white lotuses, and enjoy sporting.

verses.sloka: त्वं पौरजनवद्व्यालानयोध्यामिव पर्वतम् ।मन्यस्व वनिते नित्यं सरयूवदिमां नदीम् ॥ २.९५.१५॥
verses.transliteration: tvaṁ paurajanavadvyālānayodhyāmiva parvatam ।manyasva vanite nityaṁ sarayūvadimāṁ nadīm ॥ 2.95.15॥

translations.english: O my lovely lady Always think this river Mandakini as Sarayu and this mount Chitrakuta as Ayodhya and these wild animals as its inhabitants.

verses.sloka: लक्ष्मणश्चापि धर्मात्मा मन्निदेशे व्यवस्थित: ।त्वं चानुकूला वैदेहि प्रीतिं जनयथो मम ॥ २.९५.१६॥
verses.transliteration: lakṣmaṇaścāpi dharmātmā mannideśe vyavasthita: ।tvaṁ cānukūlā vaidehi prītiṁ janayatho mama ॥ 2.95.16॥

translations.english: With righteous Lakshmana obedient and you, O Sita, agreeable to me, you both bring me great pleasure.

verses.sloka: उपस्पृशंस्त्रिषवणं मधुमूलफलाशन: ।नायोध्यायै न राज्याय स्पृहये ऽद्य त्वया सह ॥ २.९५.१७॥
verses.transliteration: upaspṛśaṁstriṣavaṇaṁ madhumūlaphalāśana: ।nāyodhyāyai na rājyāya spṛhaye 'dya tvayā saha ॥ 2.95.17॥

translations.english: Bathing thrice in your company at the time of prayers and partaking honey, roots and fruits, I do not yearn either for Ayodhya or for the kingdom.

verses.sloka: इमां हि रम्यां मृगयूथशालिनीं निपीततोयां गजसिंहवानरै: ।सुपुष्पितै: पुष्पधरैरलङ्कृतां न सो ऽस्ति य: स्यादगतक्लम: सुखी ॥ २.९५.१८॥
verses.transliteration: imāṁ hi ramyāṁ mṛgayūthaśālinīṁ nipītatoyāṁ gajasiṁhavānarai: ।supuṣpitai: puṣpadharairalaṅkṛtāṁ na so 'sti ya: syādagataklama: sukhī ॥ 2.95.18॥

translations.english: With this enchanting Mandakini teeming with herds of deer, whose waters are drunk by elephants, lions and monkeys, decorated with heaps of flowers fallen from the trees in full bloom, who will not feel happy and free from fatigue.

verses.sloka: इतीव रामो बहुसङ्गतं वच: प्रियासहाय: सरितं प्रति ब्रुवन् ।चचार रम्यं नयनाञ्जनप्रभं स चित्रकूटं रघुवंशवर्द्धन: ॥ २.९५.१९ ॥
verses.transliteration: itīva rāmo bahusaṅgataṁ vaca: priyāsahāya: saritaṁ prati bruvan ।cacāra ramyaṁ nayanāñjanaprabhaṁ sa citrakūṭaṁ raghuvaṁśavarddhana: ॥ 2.95.19 ॥

translations.english: Rama, the perpetuator of the Raghu dynasty, describing the river Mandakini at length appropriately in this manner, wandered in the company of his beloved consort on mount Chitrakuta looking black like collyrium. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे पञ्चनवतितमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the ninetyfifth sarga in Ayodhyakanda of the holy Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
